verses.20:8: And on the other side of the Jordan he gave Bezer in the wilderness on the plain from the tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh.
verses.20:9: These are the designated cities for the sons of Israel and for the foreigner who resides among them, for anyone who strikes a person unintentionally to flee there, so that he may not die by the hand of the avenger of blood until he stands before the assembly for judgment.
verses.21:1: And the heads of the fathers' houses of the sons of Levi approached Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun, and the tribal heads of the fathers' houses from the tribes of Israel.
verses.21:2: And they spoke to them in Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, "The Lord commanded by the hand of Moses to give us cities to live in, and the pasturelands for our livestock."
verses.21:3: And the sons of Israel gave to the Levites, while receiving their inheritance, by the command of the Lord, the cities and their pasturelands.
verses.21:4: And the lot came out for the clan of Kohath; and to the sons of Aaron the priests, the Levites, there fell from the tribe of Judah and from the tribe of Simeon and from the tribe of Benjamin, by lot, thirteen cities.
verses.21:5: And to the remaining sons of Kohath, from the tribe of Ephraim and from the tribe of Dan and from the half-tribe of Manasseh, by lot, ten cities;
verses.21:6: and to the sons of Gershon, from the tribe of Issachar and from the tribe of Asher and from the tribe of Naphtali and from the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities;
verses.21:7: and among the sons of Merari according to their clans, from the tribe of Reuben and from the tribe of Gad and from the tribe of Zebulun, by lot, twelve cities.
verses.21:8: And the sons of Israel gave to the Levites, by lot, the cities and their pasturelands, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.21:9: And the tribe of the sons of Judah and the tribe of the sons of Simeon, and from the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, gave these cities; and they were designated
verses.21:10: for the sons of Aaron from the clan of Kohath of the sons of Levi, because this was the lot.
verses.21:11: And he gave them Kiriath-arba, the mother city of the Anakim, that is, Hebron, in the hill country of Judah; but the pasturelands around it
verses.21:12: and the fields of the city and its villages Joshua gave to the sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh as a possession.
verses.21:13: And to the sons of Aaron he gave the city of refuge for the one who has killed, Hebron and the lands set apart with it, and Libnah and the lands set apart beside it,
verses.21:14: and Ailom and the lands set apart for it, and Tema and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:15: and Gella and the lands set apart for it, and Debir and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:16: and Asa and the lands set apart for it, and Tanu and the lands set apart for it, and Beth-shemesh and the lands set apart for it; nine cities from these two tribes.
verses.21:17: And from the tribe of Benjamin: Gibeon and the lands set apart for it, and Gatheth and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:18: and Anathoth and the lands set apart for it, and Gamala and the lands set apart for it; four cities.
verses.21:19: All the cities of the sons of Aaron the priests were thirteen.
verses.21:20: And for the clans of the sons of Kohath, the Levites who remained from the sons of Kohath, the city of their priests was from the tribe of Ephraim.
verses.21:21: And they gave them the city of refuge for the one who has killed, Shechem and the lands set apart for it, and Gezer and the areas beside it and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:22: and Beth-horon and the lands set apart for it; four cities.
verses.21:23: And from the tribe of Dan: Elkothaim and the lands set apart for it, and Gethedan and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:24: and Aijalon and the lands set apart for it, and Gath-rimmon and the lands set apart for it; four cities.
verses.21:25: And from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Taanach and the lands set apart for it, and Jebatha and the lands set apart for it; two cities.
verses.21:26: All the cities were ten, and the lands set apart for each, those beside them, for the clans of the sons of Kohath who remained.
verses.21:27: And to the sons of Gershon, the Levites, from the half-tribe of Manasseh: the cities set apart for those who have killed, Golan in Bashan and the lands set apart for it, and Bosora and the lands set apart for it; two cities.
verses.21:28: And from the tribe of Issachar: Kishion and the lands set apart for it, and Debba and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:29: and Remmath and the lands set apart for it, and Spring of Letters and the lands set apart for it; four cities.
verses.21:30: And from the tribe of Asher: Basellan and the lands set apart for it, and Dabbon and the lands set apart for it,
verses.21:31: and Helkath and the lands set apart for it, and Rehob and the lands set apart for it; four cities.
verses.21:32: And from the tribe of Naphtali: the city set apart for the one who has killed, Kedesh in Galilee and the lands set apart for it, and Nemmath and the lands set apart for it, and Themmon and the lands set apart for it; three cities.
verses.21:33: All the cities of Gershon according to their clans were thirteen cities.
verses.21:34: And to the clan of the sons of Merari, the remaining Levites, from the tribe of Zebulun: Maan and its pasturelands, and Kadesh and its pasturelands,
verses.21:35: and Sella and its pasturelands; three cities.
verses.21:36: And beyond the Jordan opposite Jericho, from the tribe of Reuben: the city of refuge for the one who has killed, Bezer in the wilderness, Miso and its pasturelands, and Jazer and its pasturelands,
verses.21:37: and Dekmon and its pasturelands, and Mapha and its pasturelands; four cities.
verses.21:38: And from the tribe of Gad: the city of refuge for the one who has killed, even Ramoth in Gilead and its pasturelands, Kamein and its pasturelands,
verses.21:39: and Heshbon and its pasturelands, and Jazer and its pasturelands; all the cities were four.
verses.21:40: As for all the cities for the sons of Merari according to their clans, who remained from the tribe of Levi, the borders came to be twelve cities.
verses.21:41: All the cities of the Levites in the midst of the possession of the sons of Israel were forty-eight cities, and their pasturelands
verses.21:42: around these cities; each city and the pasturelands around the city for all these cities. And Joshua finished dividing the land within their borders. And the sons of Israel gave a portion to Joshua according to the command of the Lord; they gave him the city that he asked for; they gave him Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. And Joshua built the city and lived in it; and Joshua took the stone knives with which he circumcised the sons of Israel who were born on the way in the wilderness, and he placed them in Timnath-serah.
verses.21:43: And the Lord gave to Israel all the land that He swore to give to their fathers, and they inherited it and lived in it.
verses.21:44: And the Lord gave them rest on every side, just as He swore to their fathers; no one stood before them from among all their enemies; the Lord delivered all their enemies into their hands.
verses.21:45: Not one failed from all the good words that the Lord spoke to the sons of Israel; all of them came about.
verses.22:1: Then Joshua called together the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh,
verses.22:2: and said to them, "You have heeded all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you, and you have obeyed my voice according to all that he commanded you.
verses.22:3: You have not abandoned your brothers these many days; until this very day you have kept the commandment of the Lord your God.
verses.22:4: And now the Lord our God has given rest to our brothers, just as He said to them; now therefore, turn back and go to your houses and to the land of your possession, which Moses gave you on the other side of the Jordan.
verses.22:5: But be very careful to do the commandments and the law that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded us to do: to love the Lord our God, to walk in all His ways, to keep His commandments and to hold fast to Him, and to serve Him with all your mind and with all your soul."
verses.22:6: And Joshua blessed them and sent them away; and they went to their houses.
verses.22:7: Now to the half-tribe of Manasseh Moses had given a portion in Bashan, and to the other half Joshua gave a portion with their brothers on the other side of the Jordan by the sea. And when Joshua sent them away to their houses and blessed them,
verses.22:8: they went away to their houses with much wealth, and very many livestock, and silver and gold and iron and much clothing; and they divided the plunder of the enemies with their brothers.
verses.22:9: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of the sons of Manasseh departed from the sons of Israel in Shiloh in the land of Canaan to go to Gilead, to the land of their possession, which they had inherited through the command of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
verses.22:10: And they came to Gilgal of the Jordan, which is in the land of Canaan; and the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh built there an altar by the Jordan, a great altar to look at.
verses.22:11: And the sons of Israel heard it said, "Look, the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar on the borders of the land of Canaan, at Gilead of the Jordan, on the other side of the sons of Israel."
verses.22:12: And all the sons of Israel gathered together at Shiloh to go up and fight against them.
verses.22:13: And the sons of Israel sent to the sons of Reuben and to the sons of Gad and to the sons of the half-tribe of Manasseh, to the land of Gilead, Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the high priest,
verses.22:14: and ten of the leaders with him, one leader from each father's house from all the tribes of Israel; they are leaders of fathers' houses, commanders of thousands of Israel.
verses.22:15: And they came to the sons of Gad and to the sons of Reuben and to the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, and spoke to them, saying,
verses.22:16: "This is what the whole congregation of the Lord says: 'What is this trespass that you have committed before the God of Israel, to turn away today from the Lord by building an altar for yourselves, so that you become rebels against the Lord?
verses.22:17: Is the sin of Peor too small for us? For we have not been cleansed from it until this day, and there was a plague in the congregation of the Lord.
verses.22:18: And you have turned away today from the Lord; and it will be that if you rebel today against the Lord, tomorrow the wrath will be upon all Israel.
verses.22:19: And now, if your land of your possession is small, cross over into the land of the Lord's possession, where the tabernacle of the Lord dwells, and you will inherit among us; and do not become rebels against God, and do not rebel against the Lord by your building an altar outside the altar of the Lord our God.
verses.22:20: Look, did not Achar the son of Zerah surely commit a trespass regarding the devoted thing, and wrath came upon the whole congregation of Israel? And this one man alone died in his own sin.'"
verses.22:21: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered and spoke to the commanders of thousands of Israel, saying,
verses.22:22: "God, God is the Lord, and God, God Himself knows, and Israel itself will know; if in rebellion we have trespassed before the Lord, may He not rescue us in this;
verses.22:23: and if we have built for ourselves an altar to rebel against the Lord our God, to offer up upon it a sacrifice of whole burnt offerings, to offer upon it a sacrifice of deliverance, the Lord will require it.
verses.22:24: Rather, out of concern over a matter we did this, saying, 'So that tomorrow your children may not say to our children, "What have you to do with the Lord, the God of Israel?
verses.22:25: And the Lord has set the Jordan as a border between us and you, and you have no portion in the Lord." And your sons will estrange our sons, so that they do not revere the Lord.'
verses.22:26: And we said we would do this, to build this altar, not for burnt offerings nor for sacrifices,
verses.22:27: but so that this may be a witness between us and you and between our generations after us, to perform service to the Lord before Him with our burnt offerings and with our sacrifices and with the sacrifices of deliverance; and your children will not say to our children tomorrow, 'You have no portion in the Lord.'
verses.22:28: And we said, 'If it ever happens that they speak to us and to our generations tomorrow, then they will say, "Look at the likeness of the altar of the Lord, which our fathers made not for burnt offerings nor for sacrifices, but it is a witness between you and between us and between our sons."'
verses.22:29: Far be it from us, therefore, to turn away from the Lord in these present days, to rebel against the Lord by building an altar for the burnt offerings and for the sacrifices of salamein and for the sacrifice of deliverance, apart from the altar of the Lord that is before His tabernacle."
verses.22:30: And when Phinehas the priest and all the leaders of the congregation of Israel who were with him heard the words that the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh spoke, it pleased them.
verses.22:31: And Phinehas the priest said to the sons of Reuben and to the sons of Gad and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, "Today we know that the Lord is with us, because you have not committed a trespass before the Lord, and that you have rescued the sons of Israel from the hand of the Lord."
verses.22:32: And Phinehas the priest and the leaders returned from the sons of Reuben and from the sons of Gad and from the half-tribe of Manasseh, from Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the sons of Israel, and gave them the words in reply.
verses.22:33: And it pleased the sons of Israel; and they spoke to the sons of Israel, and blessed the God of the sons of Israel, and said they would no longer go up against them to war to utterly destroy the land of the sons of Reuben and of the sons of Gad and of the half-tribe of Manasseh; and they lived on it.
verses.22:34: And Joshua named the altar of the Reubenites and of the Gadites and of the half-tribe of Manasseh, and said, "It is a witness between them that the Lord is their God."
verses.23:1: And it happened after many days, after the Lord had given Israel rest from all their enemies all around, that Joshua was old, advanced in days.
verses.23:2: And Joshua called together all the sons of Israel, and their council of elders, and their leaders, and their scribes, and their judges, and said to them, "I have grown old and am advanced in days.
verses.23:3: And you have seen all that the Lord our God has done to all these nations before our face, because the Lord our God is the One who fought for us.
verses.23:4: See that, just as I told you, these nations that are left for you are in the lots for your tribes; from the Jordan I also utterly destroyed all the nations, and from the Great Sea it will border toward the setting of the sun.
verses.23:5: And the Lord our God, He will utterly destroy them from before our face until they perish; and He will send the wild beasts against them until He utterly destroys them and their kings from before your face; and inherit their land, just as the Lord our God spoke to you.
verses.23:6: Be very strong, therefore, to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, so that you do not turn aside to the right or to the left;
verses.23:7: so that you do not go in among these nations that are left; and the names of their gods shall not be named among you; you shall by no means bow down to them, nor shall you serve them,
verses.23:8: but to the Lord our God you shall cling, just as you have done until this day.
verses.23:9: And the Lord will utterly destroy them from before your face, great and strong nations, and no one has stood before us until this day;
verses.23:10: one of you chased a thousand, because the Lord our God was fighting for us, just as He said to us.
verses.23:11: And be very careful to love the Lord our God.
verses.23:12: For if you turn away and join yourselves to these remaining nations that are with you, and make intermarriages with them, and mingle together with them and they with you,
verses.23:13: know that the Lord will by no means continue to utterly destroy these nations from before your face; and they will be to you as snares and as stumbling blocks, and as nails in your heels and as darts in your eyes, until you perish from this good land which the Lord your God has given you.
verses.23:14: Now I am departing on the way, just as all those on the earth do; and you will know in your heart and in your soul that not one word has fallen from all the words that the Lord our God spoke concerning all the things pertaining to us; none of them has failed.
verses.23:15: And it will be that just as all the good words that the Lord spoke to us have come to us, so the Lord God will bring upon you all the evil words, until He utterly destroys you from this good land which the Lord has given you,
verses.23:16: when you transgress the covenant of the Lord our God which He commanded us, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them."
verses.24:1: And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shiloh, and he called together their elders and their scribes and their judges, and he stationed them before God.
verses.24:2: And Joshua said to all the people, "This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: 'Beyond the river your fathers lived from the beginning, Terah the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor, and they served other gods.
verses.24:3: And I took your father Abraham from beyond the river, and I led him through all the land; and I multiplied his offspring and gave him Isaac,
verses.24:4: and to Isaac, Jacob and Esau; I gave to Esau Mount Seir for him to inherit. And Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt, and there they became a great and numerous and mighty nation; and the Egyptians afflicted them.'
verses.24:5: And they struck Egypt with what they did to them. And after these things He brought out
verses.24:6: our fathers from Egypt, and you entered the Red Sea; and the Egyptians pursued after our fathers with chariots and with horses into the Red Sea.
verses.24:7: And we cried out to the Lord; and He put a cloud and darkness between us and the Egyptians, and He brought the sea upon them and covered them. And your eyes saw all that the Lord did in the land of Egypt; and you were in the wilderness many days.
verses.24:8: And He brought us into the land of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan, and the Lord has handed them over into our hands; and you inherited their land, and you utterly destroyed them from before you.
verses.24:9: And Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and arrayed himself for battle against Israel, and he sent and called Balaam to curse us.
verses.24:10: And the Lord your God was not willing to destroy you; and He blessed us with a blessing, and He rescued us from their hands, and He handed them over.
verses.24:11: And you crossed the Jordan, and you came to Jericho; and those who lived in Jericho fought against us, the Amorite and the Canaanite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite and the Hittite and the Girgashite, and the Lord handed them over into our hands.
verses.24:12: And He sent out the hornet ahead of us, and He sent them away from before us, twelve kings of the Amorites, not with your sword nor with your bow.
verses.24:13: And He gave you a land on which you did not labor, and cities that you have not built, and you were settled in them; and from vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant, you yourselves will eat.
verses.24:14: And now fear the Lord and serve Him in uprightness and in righteousness, and remove the foreign gods whom our fathers served beyond the river and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.
verses.24:15: But if it does not please you to serve the Lord, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve, whether the gods of your fathers, those beyond the river, or the gods of the Amorites, among whom you live on their land; but I and my household will serve the Lord, because He is holy."
verses.24:16: And the people answered and said, "Far be it from us to abandon the Lord, so as to serve other gods.
verses.24:17: The Lord our God, He is God; He brought us and our fathers up from Egypt, and preserved us along all the way in which we went, and among all the nations through whom we passed;
verses.24:18: and the Lord drove out the Amorite and all the nations living in the land from before us. Indeed, we also will serve the Lord, for He is our God."
verses.24:19: And Joshua said to the people, "You will not be able to serve the Lord, because He is a holy God, and being jealous, He will not forgive your sins and your lawless deeds.
verses.24:20: Whenever you abandon the Lord and serve other gods, He will come and afflict you and consume you, instead of how He did good to you."
verses.24:21: And the people said to Joshua, "No, but we will serve the Lord."
verses.24:22: And Joshua said to the people, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you yourselves have chosen the Lord, to serve Him.
verses.24:23: And now remove the foreign gods that are among you, and direct your heart to the Lord, the God of Israel."
verses.24:24: And the people said to Joshua, "We will serve the Lord, and we will listen to His voice."
verses.24:25: And Joshua made a covenant with the people on that day, and he gave them a law and a judgment in Shiloh before the tent of the God of Israel.
verses.24:26: And he wrote these words in a book, the law of God; and he took a great stone, and Joshua set it up under the terebinth before the Lord.
verses.24:27: And Joshua said to the people, "Look, this stone will be among you as a witness, because it has heard all the things spoken to it by the Lord, what He spoke to us today; and it will be among you as a witness in the last days, whenever you lie to the Lord my God."
verses.24:28: And Joshua sent the people away, and they went, each one to his own place.
verses.24:29: And Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who prolonged their time after Joshua and who saw all the works of the Lord, all that He did for Israel.
verses.24:30: And it happened after those things that Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died, one hundred and ten years old.
verses.24:31: And they buried him by the borders of his inheritance in Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gilead; there they placed with him in the tomb in which they buried him the stone knives with which he circumcised the sons of Israel in Gilgal, when He brought them out from Egypt, just as the Lord commanded them; and they are there to this day.
verses.24:32: And the sons of Israel brought up the bones of Joseph from Egypt and buried them in Shechem, in the portion of the field that Jacob bought from the Amorites who lived in Shechem for one hundred ewe lambs.
verses.24:33: And it happened after these things that Eleazar son of Aaron, the high priest, died and was buried in Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which he gave to him in the hill country of Ephraim. On that day the sons of Israel took the ark of God and carried it around among themselves; and Phinehas served as priest in place of Eleazar his father until he died, and he was buried in their own Gibeah. And the sons of Israel went away, each one to their place and to their own city. And the sons of Israel worshiped Astarte and Ashtaroth and the gods of the nations around them; and the Lord handed them over into the hands of Eglon, the king of Moab, and he ruled over them eighteen years.

notes.1:1: The Greek text spells Joshua's father's name "Naue" (Ναυή) for Hebrew "Nun" (and renders Joshua as Ἰησοῦς); standard modern English spellings are used here.
notes.1:4: The Greek reads "the Anti-Lebanon" rather than Hebrew "this Lebanon," omits "all the land of the Hittites," and places "from the setting of the sun" with "your borders" following "the farthest sea."
notes.1:8: The Greek reads "so that you may know how to do" (rather than Hebrew "be careful to do") and uses a third-person singular verb ("it will prosper your ways"), with "the book of this law" as its implied subject.
notes.1:10: The Greek renders Hebrew "officers" as "scribes" (γραμματεῖς), a term it also uses in 3:2.
notes.2:5: The Greek introduces the final clause with "if" (εἰ, rendered "to see if you will overtake them") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "for" ("for you will overtake them").
notes.2:11: The Greek text reads the relative pronoun "who" (ὅς, "is He who is in heaven above...") rather than the noun "God" ("He is God in heaven above..."), a textual variant likely arising from visual confusion between abbreviated Greek ΘΣ ("God") and ΟΣ ("who").
notes.2:14: In the Greek text, the men speak only the opening oath ("Our life in place of yours to death"), and Rahab speaks the second half of the verse concerning "the city," whereas in the Hebrew Masoretic Text the men speak the entire verse concerning "the land."
notes.2:19: The Greek condenses the Hebrew blood-guilt expressions ("his blood shall be on his own head... on our head") into concise legal liability terms ("liable for himself... we will be liable").
notes.3:3: The Greek distinguishes "our priests and the Levites" (and reads "the Lord our God") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "the Levitical priests" and "the Lord your God."
notes.3:4: "From yesterday and the third day" literally renders the Septuagint idiom (ἀπ᾽ ἐχθὲς καὶ τρίτης ἡμέρας), reflecting the Hebrew expression meaning "previously" or "before."
notes.3:8: The Greek text here reads "into the middle of" (ἐπὶ μέσου) the water of the Jordan, differing from the variant "into a part of" (ἐπὶ μέρους) and the Hebrew Masoretic Text "to the edge of."
notes.3:16: "Kathiairein" preserves the distinct Greek place name (related to Kiriath-jearim) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "at Adam, the city beside Zarethan"; the Greek also closes the verse with the people "stood" (ἱστήκει) opposite Jericho rather than "crossed over."
notes.4:3: Greek reads "ready stones" (hetoimous) rather than specifying the standing-place of the priests, and includes the unusual phrase "along with you and them" (hama hymin kai autois).
notes.4:11: Greek reads "and the stones" (kai hoi lithoi) in front of them, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "and the priests."
notes.4:18: "yesterday and the day before" renders the Greek idiom echthes kai triten hemeran (literally "yesterday and the third day"), meaning previously.
notes.4:24: Greek reads "the power of the Lord" (he dynamis) and "in every work" (en panti ergo), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "the hand of the LORD" and "all the days."
notes.5:1: Greek uses "Phoenicia" (Phoinikes) for Canaan here (and "Phoenicians" in 5:12), a regular Septuagint geographical rendering.
notes.5:2: Greek reads "sitting down" (kathisas), reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew verb ("sit" rather than "return/again"), and omits "a second time."
notes.5:5: Greek uniquely specifies "forty-two years" (versus forty in the Hebrew) and transliterates Hebrew midbar ("wilderness") as the place name "Madbaritis" (Madbareitidi).
notes.5:10: Greek locates the Passover "to the west of Jericho, in the region across the Jordan, on the plain," differing from the Hebrew "in the plains of Jericho."
notes.5:12: "crop" translates Greek kouran (literally "shearing" or "cutting," hence harvest or yield; some manuscripts read choran, "country"), and "Phoenicians" renders Phoinikon (for Hebrew "Canaan").
notes.6:3: The Septuagint presents a shorter form of the Lord's instructions here, omitting verse 4 entirely; in 6:5 it uniquely specifies that the city walls will fall "of themselves" (automata).
notes.6:10: "he himself announces" (autos diangeile) shifts to the third person inside Joshua's direct speech, referring to Joshua himself (cf. 6:16).
notes.6:15: Greek states that the Israelites marched around the city "six times" (hexakis) prior to the seventh circuit in 6:16, whereas the Hebrew reads "seven times."
notes.6:17: "Sabaoth" (σαβαώθ, transliterating Hebrew "hosts") is an addition in the Greek; the Hebrew of this verse reads only "to the Lord."
notes.6:26: The Septuagint adds a fulfillment notice (paralleled in 1 Kings 16:34), naming the rebuilder "Ozan" (Ozan, distinct from Hebrew Hiel), using the Greek form Abeiron (Abiram), and rendering the youngest son's name (Segub) as "the youngest who survived" (to elachisto diasothenti); "at the cost of" renders instrumental Greek en ("in/with").
notes.7:1: The Greek preserves the distinct proper names Achar (Hebrew MT: Achan) and Zambri (MT: Zabdi). "Devoted thing" (Greek anathema) denotes spoils set apart to the Lord for destruction.
notes.7:5: The Greek reads "crushed them from the slope" (rendering the Hebrew place name Shebarim as a verb meaning "crushed/shattered") and "was terrified" where the Hebrew MT reads "melted."
notes.7:7: The Greek uniquely reads "why did Your servant bring this people across the Jordan" (rather than MT "why have You brought") and "beside the Jordan" (rather than MT "beyond the Jordan").
notes.7:21: Greek psilen poikilen denotes a smooth, multicolored cloak or rug (omitting MT's "from Shinar"). "Didrachmas" renders Hebrew shekels with a Greek silver weight unit, and "golden tongue" refers to a tongue-shaped bar or ingot of gold.
notes.7:24: The Greek renders the place name as "Valley of Achor" here and also transliterates the Hebrew phrase as the proper name "Emek-achor" at the end of 7:24 and in 7:26; in 7:26, the Greek reports only the stoning of Achar himself (singular "him") without mention of burning or stoning his family.
notes.8:12: The Greek text of Joshua 8 is shorter than the Hebrew MT, omitting the second ambush of five thousand men here and all of 8:13. Here and in 8:9, "on the west" translates the Greek idiom literally meaning "from the sea."
notes.8:18: The clause "and the ambushers will rise up quickly from their place" is present in the Greek text but absent in the Hebrew MT. Greek gaisos refers to a heavy iron javelin or throwing spear.
notes.8:27: Verse 8:26 of the Hebrew MT is absent in the Greek text. Verse 8:27 omits mention of livestock and opens with an exception clause ("Except for the spoils...") linked to the destruction of Ai in 8:24-25.
notes.8:29: "Forked tree" translates Greek xylou didymou (literally "double tree/wood"), denoting a forked timber or gallows. The Greek also reads "into the pit" where the Hebrew MT reads "at the entrance of the city gate."
notes.9:1: The Greek specifies "the kings of the Amorites" and names the mountain range "Anti-Lebanon" (Hebrew "Lebanon").
notes.9:2: The Greek places the Mount Ebal altar and law-reading account (Hebrew 8:30-35) here inside 9:2; "the second law" translates Greek deuteronomion (Hebrew "a copy of the law").
notes.9:7: The Greek reads "the Horite" (ton Chorraion; Hebrew "the Hivites"); earlier in 9:4, the Greek also reads "on their shoulders" rather than "on their donkeys."
notes.9:17: The Greek names the third and fourth towns "Beeron" (Hebrew "Beeroth") and "the cities of Jarin" (Hebrew "Kiriath-jearim").
notes.9:21: The Greek omits the Hebrew's introductory "and the leaders said to them" and renders both verbs in the future tense, continuing the leaders' declaration before the closing clause "just as the leaders said to them."
notes.10:1: The Greek names the king of Jerusalem "Adoni-bezek" (Hebrew "Adoni-zedek") and states that the Gibeonites "defected" rather than "made peace."
notes.10:3: Several royal and place names differ from the Hebrew: "Elam" (Hoham), "Phidon" (Piram), "Jephtha" (Japhia), and "Dabin king of Adullam" (Debir king of Eglon); 10:5 likewise calls them "the five kings of the Jebusites" (Hebrew "Amorites"), and 10:10-11 reads "Horonin" (Hebrew "Beth-horon").
notes.10:13: The Greek credits vengeance to "God" (Hebrew "the nation"), omits the Hebrew reference to the Book of Jashar, and lacks verses 10:15 and 10:43.
notes.10:21: Literally "not one of the sons of Israel muttered [or grunted] with his tongue"; unlike the Hebrew ("none moved his tongue against any of the people of Israel"), the Greek makes "the sons of Israel" the subject.
notes.10:33: The Greek reads "Helam king of Gaza" (Hebrew "Horam king of Gezer"); in 10:40, "Nabai" and "Asedoth" reflect the Greek rendering of Hebrew "the Negev" and "the slopes."
notes.11:1: The Greek preserves distinct forms for several northern coalition names: Jabis (MT Jabin), Marron (MT Madon; also used in 11:5, 7 for MT Merom), Symoon (MT Shimron), and Aziph (MT Achshaph).
notes.11:2: The Greek reads "near great Sidon" where the Hebrew MT has "in the north," and renders MT Arabah and Naphoth-dor as Raba and Phenaeddor.
notes.11:3: The Greek places the Hittites "below the wilderness toward Maseuman" (MT "the Hivite under Hermon in the land of Mizpah") and describes both the Canaanites and Amorites as "coastal."
notes.11:8: The Greek preserves Maseron (MT Misrephoth-maim) and Massoch (MT Mizpeh); in 11:6 it likewise reads "routed" where the MT has "pierced/killed."
notes.11:16: The Greek renders MT Negev as Adeb, MT Arabah as "the land toward the west," and MT Mount Halak in 11:17 as Mount Hachel.
notes.11:19: Unlike the MT, the Greek omits the exception regarding the Hivites of Gibeon making peace with Israel.
notes.11:21: The Greek reads Anaboth (MT Anab) and "all the race of Israel" (MT "all the hill country of Israel"); in 11:22 it omits Gath and reads Aseldo (MT Ashdod).
notes.12:3: The Greek reads Hasimoth (MT Beth-jeshimoth), takes MT "from the south" as the proper name Teman, and renders MT "slopes of Pisgah" as Medoth-pisgah (following Arnon for MT Aroer in 12:2).
notes.12:5: The Greek preserves the distinct forms Sekchai (MT Salecah), Gergesi (MT Geshurites), and Machei (MT Maacathites).
notes.12:7: The Greek reads "kings of the Amorites" (MT "kings of the land") and Mount Chelcha (MT Mount Halak; cf. Hachel in 11:17), and in 12:8 transliterates MT "the slopes" as the proper name Asedoth.
notes.12:14: The Greek text lists three kings here—Hermath (MT Hormah) plus the doublet Airath and Arath (MT Arad)—bringing the enumerated kings in 12:9-24 to thirty even though 12:24 states the LXX total as twenty-nine (MT thirty-one).
notes.12:18: In 12:12-19 the Greek preserves distinct city names and groupings compared to the MT: Ailam (Eglon), Asei (Geder), Elad (Makkedah, with Bethel omitted), Ataphout (Tappuah), Aphek of Arok (combining Aphek and Lasharon into one king), and Hasom (one entry where the MT lists Madon and Hazor).
notes.12:23: In 12:20-23 the Greek preserves Symoon and Mamroth (splitting MT Shimron-meron into two kings), Aziph (Achshaph), Zakach (Taanach), Maredoth (Megiddo), Jekom (Jokneam), Eldom of Phenneddor (Dor in Naphath-dor), and Geei of Galilee (MT Goiim in Gilgal).
notes.13:3: The Greek reads "the uninhabited land" where the Hebrew names the Shihor, uses the literal Semitic idiom "on the left" for north, and reads "the Hivite" where the Hebrew has the Avvim.
notes.13:5: In verses 4-6 the Greek preserves several distinctive place names where the Hebrew differs: Teman (for "south"), Taphek (for Aphek), Galiath of the Philistines (for the land of the Gebalites), Galgaa (for Baal-gad), and Maserethmemphonmaim (for Misrephoth-maim).
notes.13:8: The opening clause ("from the Jordan as far as the Great Sea... will form the border") is a Septuagint addition extending the Lord's speech into verse 8. In verses 9-14 the Greek also reads Daidaban (for Medeba to Dibon), Acha (for Salecah), and transliterates Hebrew araboth ("plains") as Araboth (vv. 14, 26, 32).
notes.13:21: The Greek reads "the spoils of Sihon, and those who inhabited Sihon" where the Hebrew has "vassals of Sihon, who lived in the land," and in verse 22 reads "in the rout" (Greek rhope) where the Hebrew has "with the sword." Verses 17-21 also preserve Greek-distinct names: Baimon Baal, house of Meelboth, Basan, Bakedmoth, Serada, Seion, Mount Enab, Beth-thaseinoth, and Robok.
notes.13:28: The clause "they will turn the neck before their enemies, because it came to be according to their clans" is unique to the Septuagint. Verses 25-30 also preserve Greek-distinct place names: Araba, Arad, Botanei, Baan, Dibon (for Debir), Enadom, Othargaei, Bainthanabra, and Maana.
notes.14:2: The Greek reads "by the hand of Joshua" where the Hebrew has "by the hand of Moses," and in verse 3 omits the Hebrew clause explaining Moses's earlier grant to the two and a half tribes beyond the Jordan.
notes.14:7: The Greek reads "the servant of God" and "according to his mind" (third person) where the Hebrew reads "the servant of the LORD" and "as it was in my heart" (first person).
notes.14:14: The Greek reads "followed the command of the Lord" where the Hebrew has "wholly followed the LORD," and in verse 13 includes the addition "the son of Kenaz."
notes.14:15: The Greek reads "the city of Argob; this was the mother city of the Anakim" (Greek metropolis) where the Hebrew reads "Kiriath-arba (Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim)."
notes.15:1: The Greek reads Judea (likely an inner-Greek variant of Idumea/Edom) and as far as Kadesh, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Edom and at the extreme south. Throughout the boundary description in vv. 3-11, the Greek also preserves distinct place names (Ennak, Sarada, Selmona, Beth-aglaam, Taagad, Maphtho, Jebaal, Baal, Assar, Succoth, Lemna), reads the fourth part of the valley of Achor in v. 7 (where Hebrew has Debir from the valley of Achor), and translates the spring of the sun (v. 7) and the city of the sun (v. 10).
notes.15:8: The Greek reads to the south (notou), an orthographic variant of back/ridge (notou with omega, as in vv. 10-11, rendering Hebrew shoulder/slope), alongside on the south (libos, the standard Septuagint term for the south/southwest), and has land of Rephaim rather than valley of Rephaim.
notes.15:18: The Greek reads as she was going out, she consulted with him, and she cried out from the donkey, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has when she came, she urged him, and she alighted from the donkey.
notes.15:19: Instead of translating Hebrew springs of water and upper/lower springs, the Greek renders them as proper place names: Boththanis and upper/lower Gonaithlan.
notes.15:21: The Greek preserves the repeated cities in v. 21 and reflects a distinctive Septuagint list of Negev towns across vv. 21-32 (including Kaibaiseleel, Ara, Hazor, Ikam, Regma, Aruel, Hasorionain, Mainam, Balmainan, Sen, Salmaa, Seri, Baiphalad, Cholaseola, Bakok, Elboudad, Bethel, Macharim, Sethennak, Labos, Sale, and Eromoth) that differs markedly from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.15:33: Across the lowland and hill-country lists (vv. 33-58), the Greek preserves numerous Septuagint-distinct place names and totals that differ from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, including ten cities in vv. 42-44 (Hebrew has nine), Gemna in v. 46 (where Hebrew reads westward), and nine cities in vv. 55-57 (omitting Kain, where Hebrew has ten).
notes.15:59: The second half of this verse (Tekoa through Manocho, eleven cities including Ephrathah/Bethlehem) is a well-known Septuagint section absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, likely lost in the Hebrew tradition through scribal eye-skip.
notes.15:61: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text introduces a six-city wilderness district (Beth-arabah through En-gedi), the Greek omits the wilderness heading and lists seven cities across vv. 61-62 (Baddargis, Tharabaam, Ainon, Aichioza, Naphlazon, the cities of Sadom, replacing the City of Salt, and Aknades).
notes.15:63: The Greek reads to destroy them (Hebrew: to dispossess them) and until that day (Hebrew: to this day), and omits with the sons of Judah in the final clause.
notes.16:2: In 16:1-3 the Septuagint reads "Bethel Luz" in 16:1 and "to Bethel" in 16:2, and uses the distinct names Chatarothi (merging Hebrew "the Archite" and "Ataroth") and Haptaleim in 16:3 (Hebrew: "the Japhletite").
notes.16:5: The Greek reads "Astaroth and Erok" (Hebrew: "Ataroth-addar") and places Gezer (Greek: Gazara) at the end of this verse rather than in 16:3.
notes.16:6: Along Ephraim's border in 16:6-8 the Septuagint has several distinct place names: Hikasmon and Therma (Hebrew: "Michmethath"), Thenasa and Sellesa (Hebrew: "Taanath-shiloh"), Macho and Astaroth (Hebrew: "Naarah" and "Ataroth"), Taphos (Hebrew: "Tappuah"), and Chelkana (merging Hebrew "the brook Kanah").
notes.16:10: The Septuagint adds an account of Pharaoh capturing, burning, and giving Gezer as a dowry (paralleling 1 Kings 9:16), whereas the Hebrew instead states that the Canaanites became forced labor.
notes.17:2: The Greek preserves distinct forms for several Manassite clans: Jezei (Hebrew: "Abiezer"), Kelez (Hebrew: "Helek"), Jezeiel (Hebrew: "Asriel"), and Symareim (Hebrew: "Shemida," listed before Hepher).
notes.17:5: The Septuagint diverges markedly here, reading "their measured portion fell from Anassa, and the plain of Labek from Gilead" (taking Hebrew "Manasseh" and "besides" as the proper names Anassa and Labek) instead of the Hebrew "ten portions fell to Manasseh besides the land of Gilead and Bashan."
notes.17:7: The Greek preserves several distinct place names in 17:7-8: Delanath (for Hebrew "from Asher to Michmethath"), Anath (Hebrew: "Shechem"), Hiamein and Jasseib (transliterating Hebrew "southward" and "the inhabitants of" as proper names), and Thaphthoth and Thapheth (Hebrew: "Tappuah").
notes.17:9: The Greek reads "a terebinth for Ephraim in the midst of a city of Manasseh" (reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew for "these [cities]"), alongside the distinct names Karana (Hebrew: "Kanah"), Jariel, and Jaseb in 17:10 (Hebrew: "Asher").
notes.17:11: This shorter Septuagint list reads Kaithoan (Hebrew: "Beth-shean") and "the third part of Mapheta" (rendering Hebrew "the three heights [Naphath]" as "the third part" with a distinct place name).
notes.17:16: The Greek reads "choice cavalry and iron" (Hebrew: "chariots of iron") and "the valley of Israel" (Hebrew: "the valley of Jezreel"); in 17:18 it similarly reads "choice cavalry" and concludes "for you are stronger than he is" (Hebrew: "though he is strong").
notes.18:4: At the end of 18:4 and through 18:5 the Greek shifts from Joshua's direct speech into third-person narrative ("And they came over to him, and he divided...") before resuming direct address in 18:6; in 18:4 the Greek also reads "to go through" (dielthein) rather than "to divide."
notes.18:12: Along Benjamin's border in 18:12-15 the Septuagint preserves the distinct names Mabdareitis Baithon (transliterating Hebrew "wilderness of Beth-aven"), Maatarothorech in 18:13 (Hebrew: "Ataroth-addar"), and Gasein in 18:15 (Hebrew: "westward").
notes.18:16: The Septuagint transliterates Hebrew "valley of Hinnom" as Gehenna, alongside the distinct names Sonnam (Hebrew: "Ben-hinnom") and Emek-raphaein (transliterating Hebrew "valley of Rephaim"). The phrase "to the south of the Jebusite" reflects the Greek word for "south," likely an inner-Greek shift from the similar word for "back/slope."
notes.18:17: The Greek uses the distinct names Galiaoth (Hebrew: "Geliloth"), Aithamein (Hebrew: "Adummim"), and Baion (Hebrew: "Bohan," with plural "sons of Reuben"), and in 18:18 reads "to the back of the sea" where the Hebrew refers to Beth-hoglah.
notes.18:21: In the first Benjamite city list (18:21-24), the Septuagint has the distinct names Bethegaio, Amekaseis, Bethabara, Sara, Besana, Aiein, Jephratha, Karapha, and Monei; it names thirteen cities (splitting Hebrew Chephar-ammoni into Karapha, Chephirah, and Monei) while retaining the summary "twelve cities."
notes.18:26: In the second city list (18:26-28), the Septuagint has the distinct names Massema, Meiron, Hamoke, Pheira, Kaphan, Nakan, Selekan, and Gabaothiarim, includes the unusual phrase "and cities" in 18:28, and totals thirteen cities (Hebrew: fourteen).
notes.19:6: The Greek reads "and their fields" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text lists the town Sharuhen, and throughout 19:2-8 the Septuagint preserves several distinct place-name forms (including Samaa, Koladam, Harsola, Iason, Beth-machereb, Sarsusin, Batharoth, Thalcha, Barek, and Bameth).
notes.19:15: The Septuagint reads "Jericho" and "Bethman" here where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Idalah and Bethlehem. Across Zebulun's border (19:10-15), the Greek also preserves distinct geographical names such as Esedekgola, Maragelda, Beth-arabah, Sedduk, Beth-shemesh, Phangai, Gebere, Katasem, and Remmona Hamathar Haoza (treating Hebrew descriptive words as proper names).
notes.19:26: "Seion and Labanath" (Greek Seion kai Labanath) reflects the Septuagint's rendering of the coastal boundary name Shihor-libnath in the Hebrew Masoretic Text (distinct from Mount Zion); the Greek also reads Elimelech, Amiel, and Maasa for Hebrew Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal.
notes.19:29: The Greek reads "the spring of Masphassat and of the Tyrians" where the Hebrew has "the fortified city of Tyre," and in 19:35 similarly reads "the fortified cities of the Tyrians: Tyre" for Hebrew Ziddim and Zer. Across 19:18-38 the Septuagint preserves many distinct place-name forms (including Jazel, Hagin, Reeroth, Ieon, Tomman, Aimarek, Gaithbor, Salim, Saphthaibethme, Chobamasomel, Moolam, Besemiin, Hiakana, and Thessamys).
notes.19:48: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text (19:47) describes the sons of Dan capturing Leshem and renaming it Dan, the Septuagint attributes the campaign to the sons of Judah against Lachish, renaming it Lasenndak. In 19:47-48 the Greek also includes material paralleling Judges 1:34-35 concerning the Amorites in Elom and Salamin and the tribute imposed by Ephraim.
notes.19:50: The Greek reads "of God" (MT "of the Lord") and names Joshua's city Thamarchares (MT Timnath-serah; cf. Timnath-heres in Judges 2:9). In 19:49 and 19:51, the Septuagint also has "went to take possession of the land" where the Hebrew has "finished dividing the land."
notes.20:3: The Septuagint omits verses 4-6 of the Hebrew Masoretic Text, moving directly from verse 3 to verse 7 and placing the trial clause ("until he stands before the assembly for judgment") here in verse 3. "Avenger of blood" renders Greek ho anchisteuon to haima, literally "the one acting as next of kin for the blood."
notes.20:7: The Greek uses singular verbs here ("he set apart") and in 20:8 ("he gave"), making Joshua the subject rather than plural Israel as in the Hebrew, and renders Kiriath-arba as "the city of Arba" (Greek: Arbok).
notes.20:9: "Foreigner" translates Greek proselytos in its Septuagint sense of a resident alien or newcomer dwelling among Israel.
notes.21:11: Greek calls Kiriath-arba 'the mother city of the Anakim' (MT 'the father of Anak') and connects 'the pasturelands around it' syntactically to v. 12 as part of what Joshua gave to the sons of Caleb.
notes.21:14: In vv. 14-18 and 23-25, the Greek preserves several distinct city names compared to the Hebrew: Ailom (MT Jattir), Tema (MT Eshtemoa), Gella (MT Holon), Asa (MT Ain), Tanu (MT Juttah), Gatheth (MT Geba), Gamala (MT Almon), Elkothaim (MT Eltekeh), Gethedan (MT Gibbethon), and Jebatha (MT Gath-rimmon).
notes.21:20: Greek reads 'the city of their priests' (hiereon, likely an early Greek scribal shift from horion, 'borders'; cf. v. 40 and MT 'the cities of their lot'), and vv. 21-22 name only three Ephraimite cities (omitting MT Kibzaim) while stating the total as four.
notes.21:29: Greek literally reads 'Spring of Letters' (Pegen grammaton, vs. MT En-gannim, 'Spring of Gardens'); other distinct Greek city names in vv. 27-32 are Bosora (MT Beeshterah), Debba (MT Daberath), Remmath (MT Jarmuth), Basellan (MT Mishal), Dabbon (MT Abdon), Nemmath (MT Hammoth-dor), and Themmon (MT Kartan).
notes.21:34: Greek names only three Zebulunite cities, Maan, Kadesh, and Sella (MT has four: Jokneam, Kartah, Dimnah, Nahalal), leaving eleven named Merarite cities though v. 40 totals twelve; other distinct Greek names in vv. 36-38 are Miso (transliterating Hebrew mishor, 'tableland'), Jazer (MT Jahaz), Dekmon (MT Kedemoth), Mapha (MT Mephaath), and Kamein (MT Mahanaim).
notes.21:42: The second half of v. 42 is a major Septuagint addition absent from the Masoretic Text here (partly paralleling 19:49-50), recording Joshua's completion of the land division, his reception of Timnath-serah (spelled Thamnasacharath at the end of the verse), and his placement of the stone circumcision knives there.
notes.22:10: Greek reads "Gilgal" (Galgala) of the Jordan (and "Gilead" of the Jordan in 22:11), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "districts" (gelilot). Throughout chapter 22, the Greek also generally distinguishes the contested altar (bomos, vv. 10-11, 16, 19, 23, 26, 34) from the authorized altar of the Lord (thysiasterion, vv. 19, 28-29).
notes.22:19: Greek reads "small" (mikra), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "unclean" (teme'ah), and has "against the Lord" instead of "against us" later in the verse.
notes.22:20: Greek preserves the name "Achar" (matching 1 Chronicles 2:7) rather than "Achan" as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text of Joshua. Greek also lacks the negative particle in the final clause, reading "this one man alone died in his own sin" rather than "did not perish alone."
notes.22:29: Greek retains "salamein," a transliteration of the Hebrew sacrificial term shelamim ("peace offerings"), alongside its Greek equivalent "the sacrifice of deliverance."
notes.22:34: Greek credits Joshua with naming the altar and casts the statement in the third person ("between them ... their God"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the Transjordanian tribes name it in the first person.
notes.23:4: Greek reads "what I told you" (hoper eipa), likely an early Greek textual corruption from a verb meaning "I allotted" (matching the Hebrew Masoretic Text), and describes the western boundary from the Great Sea as bordering toward the setting of the sun.
notes.23:5: Greek uniquely adds that the Lord will send wild beasts against the remaining nations until He utterly destroys them and their kings, a clause absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.23:13: Greek renders the paired metaphors as "nails in your heels" and "darts in your eyes," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "a whip on your sides" and "thorns in your eyes."
notes.23:16: Greek concludes chapter 23 here without the final sentence found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text warning that the Lord's anger will burn against them and they will quickly perish from the good land.
notes.24:1: The Greek text places the assembly at Shiloh (also in v. 25), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Shechem.
notes.24:5: Here the Greek shifts from first-person divine speech (vv. 3-4) to third-person narration about the Lord (continuing through v. 13 alongside first-person plural 'our' and 'we'), omits the mention of Moses and Aaron, and reads third-person plural verbs ('they struck... they did').
notes.24:12: The Greek reads 'twelve kings of the Amorites,' whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'two kings of the Amorites.'
notes.24:31: The Greek reads 'Mount Gilead' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Mount Gaash,' arranges vv. 29-31 in a different order, and preserves an additional notice that the stone circumcision knives were buried in Joshua's tomb.
notes.24:33: The Greek concludes the book with an expanded ending—absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text—recounting the ark, Phinehas's priesthood and burial, Israel's worship of Astarte and Ashtaroth, and eighteen years of rule by Eglon of Moab (cf. Judges 3:12-14).
